subject: Kickoff: bang-bang QAOA protocol search
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the bang-bang QAOA workstream. Context: our open-source study showed that QAOA under bang-bang protocols, optimized with stochastic descent over binary protocol schedules, finds protocols whose effective p-value (~2 in the reference runs) matches the published analysis - and the search itself is a classical, embarrassingly parallel workload.

Why Meridian cares: the protocol-search machinery doubles as a general discrete-schedule optimizer, and the graphs-retrieval group has two combinatorial subproblems (index partition scheduling, cache eviction windows) where we want to benchmark it against simulated annealing.

Milestones: single-machine reproduction in April (the num_literals=10, num_clauses=10 configs), distributed search at paper scale in late June, benchmark verdict vs. annealing by 7/13.

Alina owns staffing and compute.

Anders
